note: core/skill, as a table: every SKILL.md the package's parser is asked about, and the answer it gives.

A row is a file written into a temporary directory of the harness's own; the file's absolute path is masked out of every string, so what is left is the logical name the row spells (review/SKILL.md, My_Skill/SKILL.md).

The parser is deliberately lenient where a third-party skill needs it and strict where a model reads the result: both halves are rows here, because a port that accepts more than core is the failure this table exists to catch.

A YAML library's own error text is masked after the sentence that classifies it: Go and Rust word a syntax error differently, and a contract that pinned the wording would pin the library rather than the behavior.
Not rows: the 256 KiB file cap and an unreadable file. Each is one constant or one operator sentence, not a behavior, and each is pinned by the port's own test where the constant is named.
masked: the harness's directory, in every string (metadata.path included)
an operating system's sentence after `stat <path>: ` or `read <path>: `
a YAML library's error text, after the sentence that classifies it

rows.name: invalid-utf8
rows.why: a byte that is not UTF-8 refuses the document in the YAML reader, before any field is read

rows.name: missing-file
rows.why: a path that does not exist is refused by core's own stat, which names the verb and the path; the operating system's half of the sentence is the platform's, so it is masked

rows.name: path-is-a-directory
rows.why: a directory in place of a file passes the stat and is refused by core's own read, which names the verb and the path

rows.name: scalar-int
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: an integer is its decimal spelling

rows.name: scalar-octal
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: YAML 1.1 octal: the value is 7, not the digits 007

rows.name: scalar-hex
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: YAML 1.1 hex: the value is 16

rows.name: scalar-underscored
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: YAML 1.1 underscores are separators, not characters

rows.name: scalar-uint64
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: an unsigned value past int64 is still an integer, in decimal

rows.name: scalar-overflowing
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a value past uint64 becomes a float, and is spelled at float32 precision

rows.name: scalar-float
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a plain float

rows.name: scalar-tenth
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: the shortest spelling that round-trips, not a full-precision one

rows.name: scalar-exponent-folds
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: %g drops an exponent that fits the digit count: this is 1000, not 1e+03

rows.name: scalar-exponent-kept
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: %g keeps the exponent once it outgrows the digits

rows.name: scalar-small
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a small float takes the exponent form with Go's two-digit exponent

rows.name: scalar-infinity
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a special float is Go's +Inf, not YAML's .inf

rows.name: scalar-nan
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a special float is Go's NaN

rows.name: scalar-bool
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a boolean is true, not True or 1

rows.name: scalar-yaml11-bool
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: YAML 1.1 resolves yes to a boolean, which is then spelled true

rows.name: scalar-null
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a null in a string field is the empty string

rows.name: scalar-quoted-number
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: a quoted scalar is a string and stays one

rows.name: scalar-quoted-octal
rows.why: a YAML scalar in a string field is coerced to its spelling: quoting keeps the digits YAML would otherwise resolve

rows.name: scalar-name
rows.why: a coerced name reaches the validator as the spelling: 007 is the valid name 7, and the mismatch warning quotes 7
warnings: name "7" does not match directory name "review" (accepted)
